objective.title: Close M1 with independent package gate and draft AURA adoption dossier

declared.summary: Qualify and close M1 by documenting the AURA adoption contract and seven-domain recipient matrix, re-running locked exact Math tests and standalone NuGet consumer from a local-only feed, validating all package SHA/dependency receipts, and enforcing a read-only C# release-gate validator.
declared.value: Delivers a defensible standalone Math 0.2.0-preview release gate with nine qualified product chunks, source rights, reproducible source-controlled consumer and an owner-transferable but untransmitted AURA migration/rollback request, without overstating external adoption.
debtChanges: AURA recipient adoption is not performed or asserted; the MATH-XR-002 request remains draft with transmission none, and all seven AURA consumer/test domains remain unverified.
The M1 gate records locally observed package SHA-256s; output binaries remain ignored and unpublished, and cross-toolchain bit-for-bit reproduction is not claimed.

The original AURA culture-priority resolver differs intentionally from explicit Math unit profiles; future recipient adoption must independently approve and test this semantic difference before cutover.
declared.nextAction: Refine the first M2 Math IR chunk from native and product roadmap while preserving the closed M1 gate; deliver the owner-mediated MATH-XR-002 draft to AURA only through separately authorized external workflow.

achievements.achievement: The AURA adoption question is explicitly scoped: owner-pinned Math package identities and source rights, no automatic transmission, no source removal, and full recipient compatibility review.
Seven AURA consumer families are represented with pending call-site/test inventories and no invented recipient execution; the standalone package proof and observed local hashes are linked.
The recorded M1 local extraction decision qualifies Math package availability and a draft adoption request while withholding all external adoption/acknowledgement claims.
The adoption dossier task closes with an owner-transferable draft request, a complete indicative seven-domain test matrix and a versioned local Math package contract.
Release-boundary questions distinguish local Math validation from external AURA implementation, owner rights, preserved prior references and recipient-owned rollback.
The locked solution, complete quantity tests, foundation chain, three nupkg content/dependency hashes and package-only local consumer run are independently re-observed for M1.
The local M1 gate decision records observed packages/hashes, accepted source divergences, withheld external adoption and rollback responsibilities in durable audited evidence.
The extraction boundary and rollback task closes with a re-executed local gate, verified owner rights, neutral C# gate validator, and the recipient-only migration/rollback protocol.
The AURA adoption dossier and local extraction gate chunk is completed with draft-only external request, seven-domain consumer matrix, executable gate evidence and no sibling repository mutations.
Distribution and adoption work package completes with the previously qualified package-only NuGet consumer and the independent documented M1 extraction/adoption boundary gate.

All nine exact-core product chunks and all three work packages are qualified; locked tests, local NuGet packages and isolated consumer support M1 release availability, while AURA adoption remains unstarted.
